newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 3.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said it has become the first Japanese carmaker to adopt standards set by the Japan Electric Manufacturer's Association for allowing concerted operation of different maker's machinery in factory automation systems. The machinery includes machine tools, robots and sensors.
Japan Travel Bureau (JTB) plans to open a discount airline ticket office in central Tokyo in December.
Prudential Securities (Japan) Ltd has filed charges against a former executive who it accuses of embezzling more than 2.2 billion yen in securities and cash. ----

Mitsui & Co Ltd plans to set up a joint company to develop gold mines in Uzbekistan, in cooperation with Newmont Gold Co and an Uzbekistan state-run committee for geology. After a feasibility study, the venture is expected to start gold production from the end of 1999 or the begining of 2000.

Showa Denko KK plans to boost sales of its electronics and information technology division, including sales of hard disks, by more than 80 percent from its 1996 forecast to 140 billion yen in the year of 2000 under its four-year plan starting January 1997.

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd plans to enter the liquid crystal display (LCD) and inspection equipment market, in cooperation with an Osaka-based maker of inspection equipment. Mitsubishi plans to sell the products from December.

Toray Industries Inc plans to expand sales of imported clothing to an annual 30 billion yen from the current one billion yen over the next five years. It also hopes to double sales at its international trade division to 70 billion yen in the business year starting April 1, 2000.
